rootCauseOneLine: apps/app/src/app.css sets no user-select policy at all, so every element keeps the browser default (auto) and sidebar labels, header, composer footer and hidden a11y labels all join drag selections and Ctrl/Cmd-A; only ad-hoc select-none on drag handles/menu items exists.

prReviews.topFinding: body.bb-app-shell{user-select:none} + leaf-level select-text opt-ins fixes the headline symptoms but regresses two things measured live in Chromium: a drag starting in the empty gutter beside a message no longer selects anything (works on main), and Ctrl-A on the thread paints all messages highlighted while Ctrl-C copies nothing (reduced to a standalone page: body none + selectable island + later contenteditable => empty Select All). Also leaves Info-panel directory/git status/settings text unselectable, and the branch is 66 commits behind main and CONFLICTING (ThreadPendingInteractionBanner.tsx). 129 PR unit tests pass but are class-presence/CSS-grep tests that cannot catch either regression.

proposedFix: Keep a shell-level policy in app.css (body none, editors forced to text) but make the opt-in boundary the content column (timeline scroll container incl. gutters, with tool headers/action bars set select-none inside it) instead of each prose leaf, so gutter drags and multi-message drags keep working; extend opt-in to diagnostic values (Info panel directory/branch/git status, thread title, settings ids/errors, toasts); add a real-browser (Playwright) test for gutter drag, Cmd-A+Cmd-C on content, Cmd-A from sidebar, Cmd-A in editor. The Cmd-A collapse (Blink SelectAll when the last selectable content is followed only by the composer editable and none chrome) needs one more experiment (selectable node after the composer in DOM order / user-select:contain / DOM reorder) before committing to a workaround.
caveats: Repro and PR probes were done in headless Chromium 145 (Playwright) against the web app, not the Electron desktop shell; same Blink engine and same index.html/app.css, but not verified in Electron or on macOS Cmd-A. iOS Safari behavior of the PR was not tested. The exact Blink mechanism behind the empty Select All is inferred empirically (cases B/N vs T in db-minimal-chromium5.out), not from Blink source. The worktree's HEAD was a108fa7ef (5 commits ahead of the stated base) at start; I checked out 16ceb3a54 for all base-commit work and left the worktree there.
